chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Her essential interest and giving kids a chance to perform
summary: Her community work is now primary; singing is second nature; there are no more amateur nights.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Yeah, okay. Would you say at this point that this is your essential interest?

Yeah, definitely. I mean my singing career it's second nature to me now. You know, they call me and I can go and do something. I can do no wrong, you know. So you're going to do something that challenges you and this is it. And I really feel that there is something missing so far as the kids are concerned. You see when I was young, listen, I guess I was singing every time I got a chance. There's no place for these kids to try their ways. You're either on top or not at all. And of course the business itself, I mean, I was lucky, I was discovered. I didn't have any money when I came to New York. But now you got kids that if they want to get into show business they got to start out with about forty thousand dollars or you know, get an angel. And by the time he makes the first forty thousand dollars somebody else has the money and he has had it. His career is over. This is the truth.
So we got to get a proving ground for them. And who knows, they don't have to be

And in front of an audience. There are no more amateur nights.
Yeah, you're going to do something along those lines for these kids?

Oh yeah, if possible. I mean there are a couple of theatres in the neighborhood showing horror pictures. We might get the kids on stage, you know what I mean, and have some live - we might even bring back vaudeville. I doubt it but at least we can have some fun.
